title: Allocator bucket saturation & soft OOM triage - Sable Tech
summary: Deep dive into repeated soft OOMs on private VPC deployment. Root cause hypothesis: allocator bucket saturation combined with aggressive prefetch + KV cache growth leading to transient CUDA allocation failures. Discussed mitigations: soft-oom backpressure, prefetch tuning, allocator caps, and retry semantics for stream timeouts. Agreed next steps: run reproducer with capped allocator, share telemetry dashboard, schedule pilot patch rollout next week.
next_steps: Redwood to provide patched allocator build and test harness (Leo) - due 2026-12-02
Sable to run repro with capped allocator and send logs (Jordan) - due 2026-12-03
Share dashboard with per-GPU allocator metrics and KV cache growth (Anika) - due 2026-12-01

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel, Leo Fernandez, Anika Rao (Redwood) / Jordan Miles, Priya Desai, Tom Nguyen, Ellen Park (Sable Tech)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we wanted to get into the soft OOMs you've been seeing in your private VPC cluster. Jordan sent over the traces, so Leo and i dug in this morning.
[00:20] Jordan: yeah thanks. it's been pretty noisy the last two days, we see requests fail intermittently with allocation errors, but the instance doesn't reset. it's not a device reset, more like a failed cudaMalloc at critical path.
[00:35] Leo: right, that's the soft OOM pattern — cudaMalloc returning out of memory but the GPU remains up. from the traces you sent, what's interesting is the allocator buckets fill up fast when the KV cache grows past about 18GB.
[00:50] Priya: just to be clear, we're on our private deployment, 8x A100, rosetta v2.2 of your runtime, prefetch enabled default, kv cache persistence on.
[01:05] Leo: ok good to know. couple of clarifications: when you say prefetch enabled, is that per-request or proactive sequence prefetch?
[01:12] Tom: it's proactive, we configured prefetch for longer contexts, like 8k tokens. we thought it would smooth latency.
[01:22] Leo: that can cause a lot of concurrent allocations. allocator bucket saturation happens when many similar-size allocations exhaust a particular size-class, and our current allocator then falls back to scatter/grow which triggers more fragmentation.
[01:38] Ellen: we're also seeing spikes when a canary model version is rolled; memory doesn't return to baseline for a while.
[01:45] Anika: that points to KV cache churn and incremental growth. if frames aren't trimmed or prefix caches aren't reused, you accumulate.
[01:55] Jordan: logs show lots of small frees but large retained sets; maybe fragmentation?
[02:05] Leo: fragmentation plus bucket misbalance. also, the runtime's prefetch path doesn't consult the allocator cap appropriately — it assumes allocations will succeed and keeps scheduling async copies which pile into CUDA stream and into the allocator queue. when a cudaMalloc fails, the current retry logic treats it as transient and retries with very short backoff, which exacerbates pressure.
[02:30] Maya: right — so two levers: reduce prefetch aggressiveness and improve allocator-level backpressure/retry policy.
[02:38] Priya: curious — do you think quantization affects this? we're running int8 for some models and float16 for others.
[02:45] Leo: quantization can reduce peak footprint but increases kernel temp allocations sometimes for dequant ops, so it is workload dependent. we saw both int8 and fp16 runs hit the issue at different thresholds.
[02:58] Jordan: can you explain allocator bucket saturation in simple terms?
[03:03] Leo: sure — think of the allocator as having bins for sizes: 512B, 1K, 2K, etc. if a specific bin is drained by many concurrent requests, new allocations of that size trigger larger allocations and splits that fragment memory. on GPUs that leads to many small free slots that are unusable for the next big allocation, causing cudaMalloc to fail even though total free memory might be sufficient.
[03:30] Tom: and we don't get a device reset, so it looks like app-level OOMs. makes debugging harder.
[03:38] Maya: exactly. that's why we've been calling them soft OOMs. different from a GPU watchdog reset which is a hard failure.
[03:45] [04:00] Jordan: we also observed increased PCIe transfer time when the failure windows occurred. could that be related?
[04:06] Leo: possibly, if prefetch enqueues many H2D copies, PCIe saturation adds latency and it slows freed memory reclamation. also NCCL comms for multigpu can hold onto buffers longer.
[04:20] Ellen: we're running inside a VPC with SR-IOV passthrough in place. any known interaction?
[04:25] Anika: VPC networking shouldn't directly change GPU memory behaviour, but pinned pages and driver pinned buffers used for RDMA can reduce host side memory available for staging, causing more pressure for unified memory paths.
[04:40] Priya: ok that tracks. what immediate mitigations do you recommend?
[04:45] Leo: short list: 1) temporarily cap allocator per-GPU to limit bucket greediness, 2) reduce prefetch concurrency (lower window or disable proactive prefetch), 3) enable periodic KV cache trimming after session end, 4) adjust retry policy to exponential backoff with jitter for cudaMalloc and stream timeouts, 5) collect detailed per-request allocator histograms.
[05:10] Jordan: can you do a patch for the allocator cap?
[05:12] Leo: yes, i can produce a non-invasive patch that adds a soft cap parameter; it will cause the runtime to block prefetch scheduling when the per-GPU used-by-allocator exceeds the cap and fall back to synchronous allocation with backpressure. i'll ship a build today.
[05:30] Tom: what's the risk that blocking prefetch increases tail latency significantly?
[05:35] Anika: that's why cap should be adaptive: allow small bursts but throttle if sustained growth. we can measure 95th pct before/after.
[05:45] Leo: right — the patch includes metrics emitted as tags: allocator.used_bytes, allocator.bucket_miss_rate, prefetch.pending_ops. we'll add them to the dashboard.
[05:58] Maya: any changes needed to retry semantics? the current retry seems too eager.
[06:05] Leo: current behavior retries twice with fixed 100ms intervals; that requeues allocation attempts and can create thundering herd. proposal: on allocation failures do exponential backoff starting at 50ms with cap at 2s, add randomized jitter, and if after N tries still failing return a controlled error that upstream can surface to caller as 503 with hint to retry later. also consider a fallback to a smaller model variant automatically.
[06:33] Priya: auto-fallback would be nice but we need deterministic behaviour for SLAs. can fallback be opt-in?
[06:40] Maya: yes, rollout as opt-in policy per route.
[06:45] Jordan: how about when it's a KV cache leak — would cap make us lose cached prefixes and increase token cost?
[06:52] Leo: cap and trimming policy need to be coordinated. trim least-recently-used prefixes asynchronously and respect pinned frames for active sessions. there are knobs.
[07:05] Ellen: backup question: does device fragmentation get better after a restart?
[07:10] Leo: yes, a restart usually compacts, but that's not acceptable for production. we want graceful recovery. the cap and backpressure aim to avoid restart.
[07:18] Tom: ok, runbook steps if we see this in prod?
[07:21] Maya: short-term: scale down prefetch, enable cap, trigger KV trim, watch metrics. medium-term: patch runtime, improve backoff. long-term: allocator redesign and smarter kernel-level pooling.
[07:35] Jordan: let's talk telemetry — what logs/metrics do you need to help root cause?
[07:40] Leo: please capture per-GPU free/used, allocator bucket counts, bucket miss rates, prefetch queue depth, KV cache size and counts per session, cudaMalloc latency histogram, and stream error events. sampling at 1s resolution during repro helps.
[07:55] Priya: we have perf-agent that can collect GPU counters; i'll map those to your metric names.
[08:00] Anika: i'll add allocator and KV metrics to the shared dashboard and make a time-aligned panel for the trace.
[08:08] Maya: Jordan, can you run the reproducer Michel sent earlier but with environment variable REDWOOD_ALLOC_CAP=0.85 and prefetch window 4 instead of 8?
[08:18] Jordan: yes, we'll run that. should we also enable a verbose allocator trace?
[08:21] Leo: yes, enable REDWOOD_ALLOC_TRACE=1 for a few runs; that will produce per-allocation stack traces and bucket ops but at high verbosity so only for test runs.
[08:34] Tom: any concerns about KMS or encryption or VPC that could block these changes?
[08:39] Maya: no, runtime changes are config-only, no key rotation. we will coordinate with your security team if we change collection to include call stacks. nothing persistent leaves your VPC — logs stay in your s3.
[08:52] Ellen: good. also we want an SLA impact estimate if we enable cap.
[08:57] Leo: expect slight increase in p95 on high-concurrency synthetic tests, maybe 5-10% tail increase, but far fewer allocation failures. we'll provide before/after numbers from the test harness.
[09:12] Maya: ok, recap the concrete next steps — Leo will upload patched binary and test harness and instructions, Anika will add dashboard panels, Jordan will run repros and share traces. we'll reconvene after the runs.
[09:30] Jordan: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.
[09:35] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links: patched build, dash link, and a short runbook.
[09:42] [Meeting end]
